transcript:
Header: 2026-09-30 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~43 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Sandeep Patel (Redwood SE), Ana Liu (Redwood Solutions), Maria Gomez (StratoHealth Director of AI), Alan Wright (Platform Eng), Priya Nair (Security), Tom Reed (CTO)
Links shared: network-diagram-v2 (internal link), pilot-results-2026-09 (sheet), SOC2-KMS-integration.pdf

00:00:03 Lena: ok hi everyone, thanks for joining, looks like we have most folks, wanna do quick rundown of agenda?
00:00:10 Maria: hi yep, real quick, we're tight on time this week, main things are the networking verification and the performance numbers from your last run.
00:00:18 Sandeep: yep, i ran one more pass on the model runner with the quantized profile, results are in the sheet, but i'll summarize after we cover network. some small noise in logs to call out.
00:00:28 Alan: perfect, first question — we've been trying routing through the TGW and seeing intermittent timeouts when we hit ~80% of concurrent connections, looks like UDP flaps? not 100% sure.
00:00:40 Sandeep: right, we saw that too in our lab when we hit the burst queue on the envoy proxy, sometimes packets queue and then time out, could be MTU or path-mtu issues plus iptables conntrack.
00:00:54 Priya: just to flag security side, any changes to the bastion or peering will need to go through our change window and SOC2 evidence capture, so we'll need the updated diagram and the audit log plans.
00:01:05 Lena: noted. Action for me to send updated diagram with the suggested subnets and proposed routing — i'll include the traffic flow and expected ports.
00:01:13 Tom: question on bastion: do we need a persistent bastion or just ephemeral jump boxes? our security team prefers ephemeral but ops prefers persistent for debugging.
00:01:23 Ana: ephemeral is fine for access, but for agent registration during the upgrade window a persistent jump box reduces surprises. you can do ephemeral + logging.
00:01:35 Maria: ok, can we get a proposed plan please.

00:02:10 Sandeep: back to the packet drops, in our test we had the agent kernel on v1.18 and the envoy at 1.22 — mixing versions seems to amplify conntrack pressure. upgrading the agent kernel to the latest build reduced retransmits. we recommended a short maintenance window to push the upgrade.
00:02:28 Alan: what’s the rollback plan if upgrade causes instability?
00:02:32 Sandeep: we keep the old container image available and the orchestration policy will roll back after failed health checks; also the KV cache persists across restarts so warmup is quick.
00:02:43 Priya: about KV cache — does it store any PII? our compliance team needs to know.
00:02:47 Ana: no PII is stored in KV cache, only model key/value activations and prefixes, ephemeral and encrypted at rest. we'll include an excerpt in the SOC2 artifact.

00:03:20 Maria: performance numbers — Sandeep?
00:03:23 Sandeep: yeah, so with quantization profile q4_0 and prefix caching enabled we saw a 35% reduction in p95 latency on 2k-token requests and about 28% cost reduction per token, throughput improved by ~18% for batched inference. full breakdown in the sheet but main callouts: large-context runs still need more memory; recommend increasing instance size when sequence > 6k.
00:03:45 Tom: what's the recommendation for on-prem if we want fixed latency at scale?
00:03:48 Sandeep: Dedicated nodes on our private offering with pinned GPU pools shows the best predictability. Also suggest disabling aggressive autoscale for steady workloads.
00:03:58 Maria: costs — if we bump instance for long contexts, what's the delta?
00:04:02 Lena: we'll send a short pricing addendum for the pilot extension that includes a Dedicated fallback option; that'll show delta for p3-equivalent and p4-equivalent configs.

00:04:40 Alan: back to networking specifics — TGW + VPC peering vs Transit Gateway with eBGP — which is Redwood's recommended pattern?
00:04:50 Sandeep: Transit Gateway (TGW) with route tables simplified is what we use in most pilots; VPC peering is ok for smaller setups but scales poorly. the issue you saw might be path MTU or a misconfigured NAT gateway under load.
00:05:05 Alan: we are using NAT gateway for egress; stateful rules are heavy at scale, could that be the bottleneck?
00:05:12 Sandeep: yes, large number of simultaneous connections plus conntrack limits can cause timeouts; two options — increase conntrack table and tune kernel netfilter, or move egress to a managed NAT instance fleet which is more predictable.

00:05:50 Priya: on KMS — we need to decide between us managing keys in our AWS KMS or Redwood handling key wrap; what are the implications?
00:05:58 Ana: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS keys (we never hold the unwrapped keys). If you prefer HSM-backed keys, we can integrate via your KMS and use envelope encryption. we'll share the integration doc.
00:06:12 Priya: great, please send the KMS integration doc and the checklist we can give to compliance.
00:06:19 Lena: will do.

00:07:05 Maria: any issues with model compatibility when using quantized runtime? sometimes hallucination increases slightly.
00:07:12 Sandeep: yes it's model dependent; in our testing q4_0 kept quality within acceptable delta for your eval set but we flagged a small BLEU-style shift on the legal templates. we can revert to float16 for those flows or use mixed precision select routes.
00:07:30 Tom: can we have per-route model profiles so critical flows always use higher precision?
00:07:33 Lena: yes, per-route profiles are supported — you can route by SLAs, latency, or cost. we'll add recommended config.

00:08:20 Alan: on the intermittent timeouts, can we capture tcpdump from the agent side during next test?
00:08:25 Sandeep: yes, we can enable extended debug and pull pcap; we'll coordinate a short stress window.
00:08:31 Maria: when can that be scheduled?
00:08:34 Tom: next Thursday afternoon looks open for ops.
00:08:37 Lena: i'll pencil in a 2-hour maintenance window next Thursday, propose 1600-1800 UTC, if that's ok we'll send calendar invite.

00:09:10 Sandeep: quick note on fallback routing: we tested automatic fallback to hosted model when a private node is overloaded — it works but increases egress and has higher latency. keep it as a last resort.
00:09:24 Priya: that fallback would send PII to hosted environment? can't allow that.
00:09:29 Lena: fallback can be configured to only use compatible models that meet your residency constraints; for your pilot we've disabled cross-tenant fallback, so it won't cross into hosted. we'll highlight this in config.

00:10:05 Maria: the benchmark numbers you posted — can you walk through the sheet quickly?
00:10:10 Sandeep: sure, sheet tab one has p50/p95 for sequence lengths 512/2k/6k. at 6k we saw memory pressure causing retries at 3% of requests; increasing instance to 80GB GPU memory eliminated retries. tab two shows concurrency curves, and tab three is cost per 1k tokens.
00:10:33 Alan: can you zip the logs for the retries? we've got to correlate with VPC flow logs.
00:10:38 Sandeep: yep will attach.

00:11:20 Maria: anything surprising from your side?
00:11:22 Sandeep: two surprises: one, nginx/envoy param defaults on your AMI were quite low, we increased keepalive and buffer sizes which helped. two, the model peer library had an old kernel optimization disabled; enabling it improved decode throughput by ~12%. we'll include patch notes.
00:11:40 Ana: we'll also note the version skew that caused extra logs in the agent; recommend aligning agent and controller versions before the next run.

00:12:05 Priya: audit logs — will Redwood provide JSON logs we can ship to our SIEM?
00:12:10 Lena: yes, audit logs are available as JSON; we can push to your S3 or stream to your ingestion endpoint — we'll include sample payloads in the doc.

00:13:00 Tom: what about upgrade plan — can you outline steps and expected downtime?
00:13:05 Sandeep: plan is: 1) drain traffic from one node 2) deploy agent/kernel update 3) health check 4) bring node back; rolling across pool. for a pool of 6 nodes, expect <5 minutes of reduced throughput per node, but no full outage. we recommend doing it in off-peak.
00:13:25 Maria: sounds ok.

00:14:00 Alan: for peering, do we need route tables per AZ? we want localized egress.
00:14:06 Sandeep: yes per-AZ route tables help avoid cross-AZ hops; add explicit route table entries for your TGW attachments. we'll send example terraform snippet.

00:15:12 Maria: any blockers from Redwood to proceed?
00:15:16 Lena: just the network diagram and permission for a short maintenance window; and confirmation of KMS approach from Priya. otherwise we're good.

00:16:05 Alan: timeline — after we provide the peering config, how long until you can run the stress test?
00:16:10 Sandeep: once peering is in place and firewall rules allow the agent controller, we can run tests same day; after that we'll share results within 48 hours.

00:17:00 Priya: can you confirm data at rest encryption algorithm? need AES-256 or FIPS-compliant option.
00:17:06 Ana: default is AES-256; for FIPS we can switch to an HSM-backed CMK — again we'll include that detail in the KMS doc.

00:18:20 Maria: small UX ask — can we have per-route metrics in the console for token-level cost and latency?
00:18:26 Lena: yes the Redwood Console exposes per-route dashboards; i'll add your example dashboards to the shared workspace.

00:19:10 Sandeep: quick note about model variants — you mentioned legal templates earlier, we recommend creating a dedicated route pinned to float16 to keep quality. we can show how to do that in the next demo.

00:20:05 Alan: shipping logs — we'll need guidance on log retention and PII redaction.
00:20:10 Ana: log retention is configurable; default is 90 days for pilot, but we can mirror to your long-term S3 for compliance. PII redaction can be applied at the ingestion layer.

00:21:45 Maria: ok i think we have the path forward. can we recap next steps?
00:21:50 Lena: sure — i'll send diagram and invite for maintenance window; Sandeep will run the extended bench after peering is confirmed; Priya will confirm KMS preference; Alan will provide VPC details.
00:22:05 Tom: one ask — if the kernel upgrade fails we'll need a postmortem within 24 hours.
00:22:10 Sandeep: agreed, we'll commit to that.

00:23:30 Maria: any outstanding security red flags? Priya?
00:23:33 Priya: just the KMS and fallback routing concerns; otherwise looks manageable. i'll review the SOC2 artifact once received.

00:24:40 Lena: quick note on cost — if you want to reduce p95 for large contexts without bumping instance, we can tune batching and pre-warm caches for the top N prefixes; will take a small engineering run but it's doable.
00:24:56 Sandeep: yes prefix caching for the common templates reduced cold-starts in our run.

00:26:00 Maria: anything else?
00:26:05 Alan: can you include sample terraform and route table config in the doc?
00:26:08 Lena: yes terraform snippet and envoy tuning params will be in the package i send.

00:27:20 Sandeep: one more ops note — please open an ssh bastion user list so we can pre-create keys for the test.
00:27:26 Tom: will do.

00:30:00 Maria: ok let's plan to reconvene after the maintenance window and the stress test. same time next week?
00:30:05 Lena: same time next week works, i'll send calendar.

00:31:15 Priya: on the SOC2 doc, will you include audit log examples with field names?
00:31:18 Ana: yes full sample JSON events and mapping to our schema.

00:33:00 Alan: small nit — we saw some mislabeling in the agent logs where product name printed as "Redwood Privet" instead of Private, not a blocker but thought we'd flag for debugging of transcripts.
00:33:08 Sandeep: thanks, we'll fix the naming in that build.

00:35:10 Maria: ok i think that's it. thanks everyone.
00:35:15 Lena: thanks, recap in the notes and i'll follow up.

00:35:30 End of call.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-transcribed words (e.g., "Redwood Privet"), speaker overlaps, timestamps approximate.

Attachments referenced: network-diagram-v2.pdf, pilot-results-2026-09.xlsx, SOC2-KMS-integration.pdf
